Epson QX-10
====
## CP/M; 5.25" 40-track DSDD
<!-- This file is automatically generated. Do not edit. -->

The Epson QX-10 is a Z80-based CP/M microcomputer with two internal 5.25"
double-sided drives. The drives are 48 TPI, soft-sectored, double-density
MFM at 250 kbit/s and 300 RPM, with 40 usable tracks per side (tracks
0-39). The hardware lists 80 physical tracks, but the standard formats use
only 40 per side at 48 TPI.

The QX-10 shipped with CP/M and also with Epson's Valdocs environment;
different operating system distributions used different logical geometries on
otherwise identical media, so "QX-10 format" is not a single layout.
FluxEngine distinguishes three variants found in the wild and documented in
Epson's CP/M External Reference Spec (B2.20, 24 Feb 84) and the QX-10
User's Guide (James Hansen copy), and in the QX-10 Technical Manual
Troubleshooting guide (May 83).

All variants are 5.25" DSDD, soft-sectored (single index hole), MFM,
250 kbit/s, 300 RPM, 48 TPI, 40 cylinders, 2 sides. Sector numbering is
1-based and the controller uses the normal IBM scheme.

## Options

  - Format variants:
      - `300`: 300kB 5.25" 40-track DSDD, 16 sectors x 256 bytes
      - `380`: 380kB 5.25" 40-track DSDD, 10 sectors x 512 bytes
      - `320`: 320kB 5.25" 40-track DSDD mixed bootable

## Examples

To read:

  - `fluxengine read -c epsonqx10 --300 -s drive:0 -o epsonqx10.img`
  - `fluxengine read -c epsonqx10 --380 -s drive:0 -o epsonqx10.img`
  - `fluxengine read -c epsonqx10 --320 -s drive:0 -o epsonqx10.img`

## 320kB conventional variant (16 x 256 bytes)

The layout most commonly meant by "Epson QX-10 format" in disk-imaging and
CP/M transfer utilities:

  * 40 tracks x 2 sides x 16 sectors x 256 bytes = 327,680 bytes
  * Formatted capacity listed as 328 kbyte in the QX-10 Technical Manual
    Troubleshooting guide; nominal CP/M capacity ~300 kB after reserving
    2 system tracks.

Use this for a typical QX-10 CP/M data disk if you do not know which
variant you have.

## 400kB alternate / Valdocs-associated variant (10 x 512 bytes)

Identical physical geometry and rotation speed, but each track holds
10 sectors of 512 bytes (5,120 bytes/track) instead of 16 x 256
(4,096 bytes/track):

  * 40 tracks x 2 sides x 10 sectors x 512 bytes = 409,600 bytes raw
  * Nominal CP/M capacity ~380 kB after 2 system tracks.

The Epson CP/M External Reference Spec identifies both this and the
16 x 256 layout as QX-10 formats; the BIOS listing notes the standard
implementation as 512-byte sectors with 10 sectors per track.

## 396kB mixed-format bootable variant

Some QX-10 system/boot media use a mixed organisation: early tracks use
256-byte sectors while later tracks use 512-byte sectors. The operating
system, directory and boot code occupy the early tracks.

FluxEngine's profile for this is:

  * tracks 0-1 (cylinders 0-1, both sides): 16 sectors x 256 bytes
  * tracks 2-39: 10 sectors x 512 bytes

Raw capacity with that split is 4 tracks x 4,096 + 76 tracks x 5,120 =
405,504 bytes; however, this also gives the same ~380 kB of user space,
as for the 400kB format, but with less reserved operating system space.
